headline: Bangladesh cabinet expands to 51 members, 6 new ministers and state ministers sworn in
summary: Four new ministers and two ministers of state took oath, with portfolios immediately assigned. This expansion brings the total cabinet strength to 51, including the Prime Minister.
details: Following six months in power, the Bangladesh cabinet has expanded, with six new members joining the government. Four new ministers and two ministers of state were sworn in, bringing the total cabinet size to 51 members, including the Prime Minister.

The oath-taking ceremony took place at Bangabhaban on Friday evening, administered by the newly sworn-in President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir. He himself had taken the oath as President shortly before.

Among the new appointees, Abdul Moin Khan received the Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives. Rashiduzzaman Millat, who was previously a State Minister, was promoted to Minister for Civil Aviation and Tourism.
Saching Pru Jerry was appointed Minister for Chittagong Hill Tracts Affairs, a position that had been vacant. Andalib Rahman Partho took charge of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.

Humayun Kabir, formerly the Prime Minister's foreign affairs advisor, was sworn in as State Minister for Foreign Affairs. Mohammad Shamim Kaisar (Lincoln) became the State Minister for Religious Affairs.

The cabinet now comprises 26 full ministers and 24 ministers of state, in addition to the Prime Minister. This expansion follows previous changes and additions since the government formed on February 17 after the 13th national parliamentary elections.

Saching Pru Jerry was appointed Minister for Chittagong Hill Tracts Affairs, a position that had been vacant. Andalib Rahman Partho took charge of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.

Humayun Kabir, formerly the Prime Minister's foreign affairs advisor, was sworn in as State Minister for Foreign Affairs. Mohammad Shamim Kaisar (Lincoln) became the State Minister for Religious Affairs.

headline_marked: [[Mitchell Starc sets new world record]] as Bangladesh reels at 12 for five on Day 1 of second Test
headline: Mitchell Starc sets new world record as Bangladesh reels at 12 for five on Day 1 of second Test
summary: Australia's Mitchell Starc delivered a devastating spell, taking five quick wickets, including three ducks, to leave Bangladesh struggling early in the second Test.
details: Australia pacer Mitchell Starc created a new world record and left Bangladesh in tatters, claiming five quick wickets early on Day 1 of the second Test in Mackay. Bangladesh were reeling at 12 for five after seven overs.

Starc removed Bangladesh opener Shadman Islam with the first delivery of the match, marking the fourth time he has achieved this feat in Test cricket. This surpasses West Indies pacer Pedro Collins' previous record of three opening-ball wickets.

The left-arm quick continued his onslaught, dismissing opener Tanzid Tamim and captain Najmul Hossain Shanto off successive deliveries in his second over, both for ducks. He also moved past James Anderson for the most wickets taken in the first over of a Test, with nine such dismissals.

Starc struck again in the fifth over, getting Mominul Haque for nine runs, and then removed Litton Das for a five-ball duck in the following over. This completed his 19th five-wicket haul in Tests, achieved in just 22 deliveries.

Australia had won the toss and elected to field first in the match at the Great Barrier Reef Arena. Bangladesh leads the two-match series 1-0 after their historic nine-wicket win in the first Test in Darwin.

Both teams made one change for the game, with Shoriful Islam replacing Ebadot Hossain for Bangladesh, and Matthew Renshaw coming in for Jake Weatherald for Australia. Bangladesh aims for a historic series victory on Australian soil.
